approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from scored survivors. It fits a fixed tree regressor to every ordered pair of accepted molecules using their count fingerprints and raw score differences. To predict a new offspring, it adds each accepted molecule's score to that reference's predicted difference and averages every reference equally. This all-reference location replaces the mean in the existing Gaussian-process sampling rule; the original correlated residual and Gaussian-process mean eligibility rule still decide which eligible sampled maxima are purchased. Only real accepted feedback updates the archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add bidirectional reciprocity at every accepted reference: take half the forward prediction minus the reverse prediction before the existing uniform average. This removes the symmetric part of the difference predictor without changing its training. The earlier correction applied reciprocity only at one incumbent and slightly improved error while losing endpoint score; the Parent's separate all-reference change improved both measured error and its code-Parent endpoint. Their combination has not been evaluated. No completed Child of this all-reference Parent has tested it, and the other scheduled siblings investigate different predictor or residual consumers. The new test asks whether reciprocity still improves complete paid prediction after reference averaging and reaches different real purchases.

observed_bottleneck:
The limiting behavior is residual raw-direction inconsistency inside the actual code Parent n-ff10f4d5e7f3's all-reference predictive location. Its all-reference mechanism is confirmed, with falsifier not_triggered: 435 fits and 4350 paid joins, 364 changed purchase sets and 784 actual-only identities versus its passive incumbent rule. Complete same-paid MSE is 0.008649387924947863 versus incumbent 0.00918329073879438, favorable in 11 cells and adverse in 4, but the original GP remains more accurate at 0.0054658416803000385. The uncorrected pool diagonal and swap absolute means remain 0.017277698110454324 and 0.02472629956298779. These are measured defects, not identified causes of endpoint loss. The complete code-Parent macro rises from 0.5248434366619207 to 0.5470301211919261 (population SD 0.024079340089135263), delta +0.022186684530005312, with all three seed deltas positive, 10 favorable and 5 adverse endpoint cells. Preserve that conditional positive result.

The distinct source n-93efcfa0f760 applied the two-direction projection only at its single incumbent. It completed 4350 joins and changed 357 sets/737 paid identities; MSE fell from 0.009277923499679742 to 0.009206697926852135, with 5 adverse predictive cells, yet its separate complete code-Parent macro delta was -0.0038813612303220113 (5 favorable/10 adverse endpoint cells). Its confirmed mechanism and triggered endpoint falsifier coexist. Its correction-only purchases had worse projected error, so the pooled gain is not evidence that displaced purchases were better. The original n-7e9f57600099 D-versus-GP prediction remains refuted in every Search cell; it is not a failed execution or an inherited useful-prediction capability. Finalized policy records give task_safe=true for the all-reference Parent and false for the single-reference correction and raw cardinal ancestor; the older reports' unavailable flags are not new missing margins.

The frozen formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de remains mean 0.607030316211131. Its original literal c-matched-endpoint-gain criterion and the ancestor's lock-mismatched comparison remain unchanged. A different-Parent gain cannot attain that criterion. The new combination is justified by complete all-reference support plus implemented reciprocity arithmetic, not by summing sibling deltas or assuming that reciprocity repairs remaining rank/cycle error.

hypothesis: Extend the code Parent's all-accepted-reference location by a two-direction reciprocity projection at every reference, keeping its fitted raw cardinal regressor D(i,x) oriented as y_x-y_i. For each actual pool candidate x and every chronological real accepted reference i, obtain native float32 D(i,x) and D(x,i), cast each operand separately to float64, and compute A(i,x)=(float64(D(i,x))-float64(D(x,i)))*0.5. Add the same raw reference score y_i and use the Parent's serial-order float64 left fold divided once by n to obtain mu_recip(x)=mean_i[y_i+A(i,x)]. The unchanged raw all-reference mu_raw(x)=mean_i[y_i+D(i,x)] becomes a passive same-state comparator. This removes the symmetric directional component for all reference consumers; it does not constrain triangle cycles or fit a scalar potential. Retain the original count-GP residual R and original-GP-mean eligibility; active sampled values are mu_recip+R. The causal prediction is exact self/swap consistency together with candidate-varying location and actual purchase exposure, followed by strictly lower raw-score MSE than mu_raw on the complete actual Child paid stream. Calibration, ordering, real feedback and endpoints are measured separately. No neural training, learned weights, support selection, cycle penalty/projection, GP blending or parameter change is part of this mechanism.

finding_summary.headline: Reciprocity ran correctly, but raised paid prediction error and lowered endpoints
finding_summary.insights: Exact reciprocity is insufficient to improve this all-reference predictor: the borrowed bidirectional averaging formula operated, but its complete paid-stream accuracy prediction was contradicted. Neural training, independent-reference noise reduction and longer-loop constraints were not tested; the retained tree learner and GP uncertainty are explicit adaptations. The all-reference Parent's earlier improvement and the raw cardinal ancestor's prediction refutation remain intact. This result settles the registered combined-inference prediction under this host, without deciding the fate of the broader approach or assigning separate effects to averaging and reciprocity. The method still has a predictive-ranking limitation: tie-half ordering accuracy on the actual paid batches was 0.652176 for the reciprocal law, 0.648019 for the raw law and 0.702474 for the original GP. The modest ordering gain over the raw law coexists with worse squared error and lower endpoints. Correct algebra does not make the pair model a better guide to these paid outcomes; a different predictor or ranking model could address that limitation, but was not evaluated here. Molecular evidence also shows uneven local breadth: aggregate generic scaffold variety rose from 1,240 to 1,290, yet two sessions had only two generic scaffolds among their 29 highest-scoring purchases. Large linked assemblies, unusual neighboring bond environments and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Coherent core/linker replacement is the kind of proposal operator that could address that separate limitation; these observations establish neither a chemical cause of the score loss nor the value of a new filter or reward. All 2,175 late purchases are retained. The 150 terminal rows have measured scores, prediction errors and survivor outcomes, but no subsequent fit or breeding opportunity; they are not failed or missing purchases. Passive alternatives have no unpurchased rewards or adaptive endpoints. Shared seeds, initial records and genealogies do not provide independent replication or causal mediation, and the joint result does not separately price retained GP, graph, archive or gating components.
finding_summary.results: All 15 sessions completed their 300-call budgets. The 435 fits and 435 pools used every accepted reference in both directions; reconstruction found exact zero projected self and swap defects while retaining nonzero raw defects. All 435 pools had candidate-varying displacement, and 348 purchase sets changed, introducing 599 paid identities outside the passive raw all-reference sets. On all 4,350 purchases, reciprocal raw-score MSE was 0.008314474808, above the unchanged raw law's 0.008247490354; the increase was 0.000066984454. Ten task/seed cells improved their error and five worsened, including all three docking cells. The original GP remained more accurate at 0.005213849635. The preregistered predictive falsifier therefore triggered after correct execution and real choice exposure. Mean endpoint score fell from 0.547030121 to 0.529117998, a paired change of -0.017912123; 12 of 15 cells and two of three seed macros declined. This also failed the separate +0.002 developmental endpoint target. The formal Anchor criterion is inapplicable because this node has a different code Parent.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic analogues and polyamine cages, with uneven size, unusual bond environments and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All 15 original Child and 15 published code-Parent Search trajectories were read for frozen seeds 0/1/2. Each node supplies 4,350 accepted optimizer purchases and 150 supplied initial observations. All 300 rows per cell are retained in the audits; chemistry aggregates below exclude initials. This is the purchased output, not the unmeasured set of generated or unpurchased pool members. No issued path is missing and no task is omitted. The issued context separately confirms child_complete=true and paired_complete=true against code Parent n-ff10f4d5e7f3, with all three matched Search seeds and no profile mismatch. No held-out or Confirmation outcome is used. These are largely cyclic aromatic structures containing heteroaryl carbonyls, amides/lactams, ethers, halogenated aryl groups and cyclic amines; some sessions instead accumulate large linked assemblies or complicated fused/bridged cores. Digest SMILES-text ring-closure rates are 0.9943–1.0 and aromatic-presence rates are 0.9885–1.0. The separate RDKit reading finds aromatic atoms in 4,335 purchases and eight acyclic purchases. Child heavy-atom median/range are 32 and 3–120; Parent values are 33 and 1–120. Counts at the retained source-defined boundaries <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 heavy atoms are 8, 8, 642 and 638, versus 8, 8, 607 and 597 in the Parent. The large tail is uneven: one covered task contributes 548 of the Child >=50 cases. These are diagnostics, not size limits or rewards. There are 1,985 typed and 1,290 generic Murcko scaffolds, versus 1,969 and 1,240 in the Parent, including the empty acyclic scaffold. Aggregate variety coexists with closely related local analogues; the diversity chip does not claim a single global collapse. Radius-2 chirality-aware 2,048-count Morgan dot-product Tanimoto, pair-weighted only within task/seed sessions, is 0.646919 versus 0.652628; excluding <=6-heavy-atom fragments gives 0.649155 versus 0.654981. Within actual ten-purchase batches the corresponding values are 0.744649/0.746456, or 0.747202/0.749127 after fragment exclusion. No cross-session pairs are formed and shared initial records or genealogies do not become independent replication. The Child contains N–halogen bonds in 868 purchases, O–halogen bonds in 200 and O–O bonds in 255; Parent counts are 760, 125 and 59. It also has 220 structures with a perceived cycle of at most four atoms whose atoms all carry aromatic flags, and 327 with a perceived ring of at least nine atoms; Parent counts are 294 and 373. These graph features require chemical scrutiny, but do not measure strain, stability or synthesizability. The historical generic cumulene SMARTS matches any two consecutive double bonds, including sulfonyl sulfur. The supplemental atom-centred counts separate 193 carbon-centred cases from 157 sulfur-centred cases, versus 276 and 341 in the Parent; ordinary sulfonyl groups are not called liabilities merely because the generic flag fires. All 4,350 Child purchases lack assigned tetrahedral configurations and specified double-bond geometry, despite 7,394 unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,888 molecules; Parent values are 6,666 centres in 2,672 molecules. Only one Child purchase has formally charged atoms. Neutral depictions do not establish solution protonation states. Synthetic plausibility is questionable because recognizable functional groups coexist with unusual heteroatom bonding, unspecified geometry and complex ring junctions; no synthesis or conformer feasibility was measured. The weak drug-likeness chip is a structural reading, not an ADME, toxicity or biological-utility result. Top-87/bottom-87 subsets below use the supplied scores among 870 purchases per task with fixed seed/evaluation tie ordering; the per-cell analogue is 29 purchases. These subsets describe chemistry and do not rank or select Algorithm Nodes. All inherited Parent aggregate and task descriptors were recomputed and exactly matched its immutable prior audit after JSON normalization. Chemistry associations do not decide mechanism activation, mediation, score attribution or method selection. Methods, complete records and provenance: policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json; policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/inspect_chemistry.py; policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/assemble_chemistry_summary.py; policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/original-input-mapping.json; policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/inspect_chemistry.py; policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json; policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/bond-context-audit.json; nodes/n-ff10f4d5e7f3/molecular.json. Current completeness authority: policy/requests/r0073-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-28a067308e22f6f0.json#context.comparison. Each task cites its paired audits and underlying trajectories below.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 purchases have 3–51 heavy atoms, median 25, with a median of three perceived rings. The leading seed-0 structure is a 24-heavy-atom pyridyl/fused aza-aromatic system carrying an allene, methoxy and N–F substitution. Seed 1 reaches a high-scoring 25-heavy-atom aryl carboxamide on a small unsaturated fused ring, with N–F and N–S decoration. Seed 2 instead reaches a 25-heavy-atom bridged unsaturated core bearing an N-hydroxy hydrazide and bromophenyl group. These are distinct local families, with conventional aryl/amide fragments embedded in questionable bond and junction environments. The top-87 set has 15 typed/seven generic scaffolds, compared with 13/four for the Parent; the complete Child set has 302/145. Initial supplied chemistry already includes aromatic amides, so these are elaborations of represented motifs, not evidence of discovering a new pharmacophore. Evidence files: policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/original-input-copies/child/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-ff10f4d5e7f3/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/original-input-copies/child/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-ff10f4d5e7f3/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0073-00-improve-L01/molecular/original-input-copies/child/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-ff10f4d5e7f3/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: Carbon-centred cumulated double bonds occur in 164 purchases, including 36 of the top 87; N–halogen bonds occur in 295, including 46 of the top 87. Neither flag alone proves instability, but the score does not certify these unusual environments.
The highest-scoring bridged hydrazide has two unassigned tetrahedral centres. Specified stereochemical and double-bond configurations are absent from the purchased set.
missing_features: Compact alternatives retaining the favorable aryl/heteroaryl scale while using more conventional carbonyl, amine and unsaturation environments are not broadly represented among the leading local analogues.
The trajectories do not identify a unique missing pharmacophore or show that the extra unsaturation or N-halogen decoration is necessary; matched chemical alternatives are missing from this evidence.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-leading scores 0.431936581, 0.417398755 and 0.426005820 occur at 24–25 heavy atoms. The quoted low examples include 47- and 51-heavy-atom aryl/amide assemblies at approximately 2.31e-19 and 5.63e-23, and a three-heavy-atom ether at approximately 3.56e-16. The top-87 size interval is 23–26 atoms. The visible gradient therefore favors a restricted molecular scale and particular local heteroatom/unsaturation arrangements over either fragmentation or large recombination products. Carbonyls occur in only 51 of the Child top 87 versus all 87 Parent examples, so an amide is not a universal explanation. All three Child endpoint contrasts are adverse even though generic scaffold breadth increases. Supplied best scores in seed order 0/1/2 are Child [0.431936581, 0.417398755, 0.426005820] and Parent [0.460926196, 0.459752042, 0.451975321]; the issued paired differences are [-0.028989615, -0.042353287, -0.025969500]. These are descriptive endpoint associations, not chemical causation or component attribution.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need coherent core and linker replacements that preserve useful neighboring functional groups and overall molecular scale without requiring repeated fragment growth. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
